This caps Block Limit Registers at 1, yielding 12.5% occupancy. Three prior autotune attempts all crashed. The crash root cause is that kernel_function() explicitly passes BLOCK_M=BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N=BLOCK_N, num_warps=8, num_stages=1 as keyword arguments to the kernel launch, which OVERRIDES the autotune-selected values — Triton raises a TypeError when autotune tries to set a constexpr that was already provided as a kwarg. The fix: (1) add @triton.autotune above @triton.jit with configs that always include BLOCK_D=1024 and NUM_D_BLOCKS=1 as fixed constexprs passed at launch site, (2) remove BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, num_warps, num_stages from the explicit kernel_function() launch call so autotune controls them, (3) use a lambda grid so BLOCK_M is read from meta, (4) keep BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N <= 32 to avoid SRAM overflow with BLOCK_D=1024.
